oneLiner: A trapped-ion quantum computing company that has bought its way into a full stack - chip design, a US foundry, networking, sensing and now security software. The market is betting that sold-out system orders turn into a billion-dollar revenue line before the cash raised from shareholders runs down.

verdict.stance: Neutral - real demand, funded by dilution
verdict.summary: The Q3 print was the strongest evidence yet that demand is real: backlog doubled, next-generation systems are sold out for 2027 and DARPA and NVIDIA both picked IonQ. But nearly two-thirds of the revenue step-up was the acquired foundry, every dollar of revenue still costs about $2.50 of operating loss, and the bill is paid in new shares and warrants. Our probability-weighted value sits roughly at today's price before counting 2027 cash burn and further share issuance, so the stock already pays for our base case and the upside depends on the bull path. We would turn positive if Platform revenue keeps growing sequentially without SkyWater's help and adjusted EBITDA losses narrow as guided; we would turn cautious if Q4 Platform revenue falls back, Superion 256 deliveries slip out of H1 2027, or another large equity raise follows.
wtb: FY2027 revenue reaches about $1.0B or more, roughly double the FY2026 guide, with IonQ Platform (not the foundry) supplying more than half of it.
Superion 256 systems start shipping in H1 2027 and remaining performance obligations stay above $1.2B at Dec 31, 2026 even as backlog converts.
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrows from Q3 2026's $133.6M in Q4 2026 and keeps narrowing through 2027, so the $3.7B lasts without another raise before 2028.
Revenue compounds near 68% a year for eight years (the computed reverse-DCF hurdle) - mostly organically, since the +127% a year of the last three fiscal years leaned on acquisitions.

bear.why: Superion 256 deliveries slip and lumpy government deals pause: Platform grows only ~35% to ~$0.41B and SkyWater runs slightly below its Q3 pace (~$0.44B). With losses still near $0.5B a year and half the mix a low-margin foundry, the market stops paying a quantum scarcity premium and values the blend at ~6x sales.

base.why: Backlog converts on schedule: Platform grows ~75% to ~$0.53B on Superion 256 shipments, SkyWater holds its ~$0.5B annualised pace and Elisity adds a little. Adjusted EBITDA losses narrow but stay large. The market pays ~12x sales - a premium multiple, but well below what it paid on pure-play revenue, because growth halves and the foundry dilutes margin.

bull.why: Extra system capacity is added, DARPA Stage C and NVIDIA deployments pull in follow-on orders and Platform more than doubles to ~$0.72B, with SkyWater's quantum foundry lines growing. A visible path to break-even and order books filling into 2028 let the market pay ~20x sales for the only scaled, vertically integrated quantum platform.

scenarioModel.note: Value per share = (FY2027 revenue x EV/Sales + net cash) / shares. The page adds the latest net cash it carries (~$3.2B, i.e. after the October 2026 offering) and divides by today's ~465M shares. Roughly: bear ~$18, base ~$34, bull ~$63. Not modelled, which flatters every case: cash burn to end-2027 (the TTM burn was $689M, about $1.50 a share) and further dilution from stock compensation, the Elisity shares if not yet in the count, and warrants. Revenue splits (SkyWater ~$0.5B from annualising two months of $83.5M; Platform ~$0.30B in FY2026 by subtraction from the guide) are Siberforge estimates, not company figures or consensus. Management has given no FY2027 guide.

debates.q: How much of the growth is IonQ's own, and does it carry into 2027?
debates.bull: IonQ Platform revenue grew 127% YoY in Q3 2026 to $90.3M, management lifted FY2026 quantum computing growth to more than 110% from 100%, and Platform signed about $290M of new contracts in the quarter - more than three times the segment's revenue.
debates.bear: SkyWater supplied $83.5M, or 62% of the YoY dollar increase, from only two months of ownership; no organic rate was given for Q3, and the 127% still includes businesses bought since 2024. If SkyWater holds its Q3 pace for a full quarter (~$125M), the FY2026 guide midpoint leaves only ~$66M for Platform in Q4, a sequential decline (Siberforge arithmetic).
debates.view: The growth is part earned, part bought, and the Q4 guide is either conservative or says Platform is lumpy. The computed check shows the price needs ~68% a year for eight years; acquisitions cannot supply that, so Platform alone has to. We give credit for the bookings but want one more quarter of sequential Platform growth before paying for more than the base case.

signpost.metric: Q4 2026 IonQ Platform revenue and the first FY2027 revenue guide
signpost.threshold: Platform at or above Q3's $90.3M and a FY2027 guide of $1.0B or more = base case intact; Platform below ~$75M or a guide under $0.9B = bear case gains weight
signpost.when: Q4 2026 report, late Feb 2027 (date not announced)

debates.q: Does $3.7B buy a path to self-funding, or only time and more dilution?
debates.bull: Pro forma cash and investments of $3.7B exceed the combined resources of the listed pure-play rivals; the CFO guided Q4 adjusted EBITDA to improve on Q3, called about $40M of Q3 G&A one-time integration cost, and said profitability programs and site consolidation start in 2027.
debates.bear: Every computed quality row is red: TTM operating cash flow was -$645M against reported net income of +$255M, and that profit exists only because warrant liabilities fell with the share price (TTM operating income was -$1.3B). Q3 operating cash outflow alone was $315.5M. Diluted shares rose 36.1% YoY before October's 50M shares and pre-funded warrants.
debates.view: The runway question is answered for now; the dilution question is not. The computed net cash of $915M and ~1.6-year runway is struck at Sept 30 and counts only cash and short-term investments; adding long-term investments and the offering gives roughly five years at the TTM burn, but under three at Q3's pace. Management raised with $1.7B already in hand, which tells us it will keep choosing shares over restraint. We treat the reported GAAP profit as noise and judge the company on adjusted EBITDA and operating cash flow.

signpost.metric: Q4 2026 adjusted EBITDA loss and operating cash flow; any new equity or warrant issuance
signpost.threshold: loss at or inside the ~$124-127M the CFO endorsed and quarterly operating outflow back under $200M = constructive; a wider loss or another raise in H1 2027 = cautious
signpost.when: Q4 2026 report, late Feb 2027, and through mid-2027

debates.q: Can IonQ build and ship what it has sold?
debates.bull: Owning the fab is working: six months in, wafer lots for 256-qubit chips are up twelvefold and tape-out cycles more than three times faster; the CEO says chips are not the constraint and that order books are filling into 2028.
debates.bear: All Superion 256 capacity for 2027 is already sold, so 2027 system revenue is capped by how fast IonQ scales whole-system assembly and commissioning, something it has never done in volume. Management declined to give a 2027 unit number, and RPO timing was not disclosed.
debates.view: Sold-out is good news about demand and a warning about supply. The base case needs first Superion 256 shipments in H1 2027 as management indicated; a slip into H2 moves revenue into 2028 and hands the bear case its ~35% Platform growth.

signpost.metric: First Superion 256 deliveries (NVIDIA research center, Florida International University, SDT) and RPO
signpost.threshold: at least one system delivered and accepted by mid-2027 with RPO above $1.2B = on track; no delivery by Q2 2027 results = bear case
signpost.when: Q1 and Q2 2027 reports (May and Aug 2027)

thesis: Demand is contracted now. Platform backlog rose from $485M to $689M in one quarter, about $180M of the new contracts were quantum computers, and 2027 Superion 256 capacity is sold out (debate 3).

Independent validation arrived. IonQ is the only trapped-ion company advanced to Stage C of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, with potential program value up to $300M, and NVIDIA chose a Superion 256 as the first on-premise quantum computer at its Accelerated Quantum Research Center.

The foundry is a strategic asset as well as acquired revenue. SkyWater kept and extended D-Wave, signed Qolab, grew its outside quantum foundry revenue more than 30% YoY and rests on a multi-year take-or-pay supply agreement with Infineon.

No pure-play rival can match the balance sheet. Pro forma liquidity is hundreds of times the quarterly revenue of D-Wave or Rigetti, which lets IonQ fund a new system generation every year and keep buying adjacent businesses (debate 2).

The customer base is broadening. In Q3 2026 commercial customers were roughly 65% of Platform revenue, international about 35% and multi-product customers 40%, with nine sensing contracts signed since July.

latestQuarter.label: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30, 2026; reported Nov 5, 2026)
points: Revenue $173.8M, +336% YoY; consensus was ~$137-141M depending on source. IonQ Platform $90.3M (+127%); SkyWater Foundry Services $83.5M from two months of ownership.
GAAP operating loss $433.1M, including $146.9M of stock compensation and $127.6M of depreciation and amortisation; adjusted EBITDA loss $133.6M (vs $48.9M a year earlier); adjusted EPS -$0.29.
GAAP net income $564.0M ($1.35 diluted) only because of an $896.2M non-cash gain on warrant liabilities.
Cash and investments $1.7B at Sep 30; $3.7B pro forma for the $2.0B equity offering that closed Oct 16, 2026.
After the quarter: Elisity (zero-trust security software) acquired for $1.15B in stock at closing, plus up to $150M of earn-out through Jan 2028.

latestProse: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30; reported Nov 5). Revenue of $173.8M rose 336% YoY and beat consensus of roughly $137-141M, the first quarter reported in two segments: IonQ Platform $90.3M and SkyWater Foundry Services $83.5M (the deal closed Jul 31, so two months, net of inter-company work). Gross profit before depreciation was about 22% of revenue (Siberforge calculation from the filing), down from about 25% in Q2 as the foundry entered the mix. The GAAP operating loss widened to $433.1M and the adjusted EBITDA loss to $133.6M; the $564.0M of net income is a non-cash warrant gain. Operating cash outflow was $315.5M in the quarter, with about $40M of one-time integration cost in G&A. Since the print, IonQ closed the all-stock Elisity purchase; the $2.0B October raise sold 20.5M shares and 29.5M pre-funded warrants at $40.00 to a Heights Capital entity, plus seven-year warrants on 100M shares at $69.46.
guidanceProse: FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to $505-515M from the $450-460M set at the Sept 8 Investor Day (the August standalone guide of $280-290M excluded SkyWater). Nine-month revenue was $318.5M, so the midpoint implies about $191M in Q4. Quantum computing revenue is now expected to grow more than 110% in FY2026, up from 100%. On adjusted EBITDA the CFO said Q4 should improve on Q3 and called consensus of roughly -$124M to -$127M not unreasonable. No FY2027 guidance was given; management spoke of heading to $1B of revenue without a date, and whether the FY2026 range includes Elisity was not stated.

guide.label: FY26 rev guide (raised Nov 5)
guide.sub: from $450-460M (Sept 8) | implies Q4 ~$191M | Q4 adj. EBITDA loss ~$124-127M

segments: IonQ Platform: quantum computers (Forte Enterprise, Tempo, Superion 256 from 2027) sold as systems and as cloud access, plus quantum networking (ID Quantique, Qubitekk, Nexus Photonics), sensing (optical atomic clocks) and security; Elisity's zero-trust software joins from Nov 2026.

SkyWater Foundry Services: US chip foundry consolidated from Jul 31, 2026 - quantum foundry (D-Wave, Qolab), secure manufacturing for defence customers and a CMOS business anchored by the Infineon take-or-pay agreement. External revenue only; work for IonQ's own chips is eliminated.
competitive: D-Wave (QBTS): Q3 2026 revenue $4.5M (+21% YoY), RPO $38.3M; annealing-first, and now a multi-year customer of IonQ's SkyWater foundry.
Rigetti (RGTI): Q3 2026 revenue $1.4M (-28% YoY, per secondary coverage); superconducting gate-model; Commerce Department R&D deal for up to $100M.
IBM: the gate-model scale benchmark, targeting the fault-tolerant Starling system for 2029. Google opened early access to its 105-qubit Willow chip in March 2026.

The comp set widened in 2026: IQM listed in July (26 systems sold, 17 delivered at the time), Quantinuum and Infleqtion began public reporting in August, and Intel plans to buy quantum software firm Classiq for about $2.3B.
moat: Capital, roadmap velocity and vertical integration: the deepest balance sheet among quantum pure-plays, trapped-ion two-qubit fidelity of 99.99% (2025), its own chip design (Oxford Ionics) and a US foundry that rivals also depend on. What is still missing is proof of commercially valuable quantum advantage; today's revenue is early-adopter systems, cloud access, networking and sensing gear and foundry wafers, not a defensible installed base.
risks: Shareholders pay for the growth. Diluted shares rose 36.1% YoY to 401M in Q3 2026 before the October raise (50M shares and pre-funded warrants, plus 100M warrants at $69.46) and the $1.15B all-stock Elisity deal; stock compensation of $146.9M was 85% of the quarter's revenue (debate 2).

Reported profit is an accounting artifact. TTM net income of $255M sits beside TTM operating income of -$1.3B and operating cash flow of -$645M; warrant liabilities fall when the share price falls, so GAAP earnings look best when holders do worst.

Losses scale with revenue. Operating margin was -249% in Q3 2026 after -421% in Q2, an improvement that came from adding foundry revenue at a ~22% gross margin, not from operating leverage; adjusted EBITDA loss was still larger than a year earlier by $85M.

Most of the step-up was bought. SkyWater was 48% of Q3 revenue, and six-plus acquisitions since 2024 are being integrated at once, with more back-office systems and sites than the company says it needs (debate 1).

Trapped ions may not win. IBM, Google and neutral-atom rivals scale qubit counts faster, and DARPA's final stage is a test IonQ can still fail; if error-corrected utility arrives on another architecture first, the backlog is early-adopter spending, not an installed base.
catalysts: Late Feb 2027 (date not announced): Q4 2026 report and first FY2027 guide - Platform revenue vs Q3's $90.3M, adjusted EBITDA vs ~-$124-127M (debates 1, 2).
H1 2027: first Superion 256 deliveries, with NVIDIA's research center described as one of the earlier ones (debate 3).
Through 2027: DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Initiative Stage C evaluation and any awards under the up-to-$300M program (debate 3).
Any new financing or acquisition: size and form of payment are the direct read on debate 2; Elisity earn-out runs through Jan 2028.

valPresets.note: Deeply unprofitable (TTM cash burn about $689M through Sep 2026), so revenue mode with a horizon FCF margin and exit multiple is the only workable frame. TTM revenue holds just two months of SkyWater, so growth rates here start from an understated base. Interim burn and future dilution are ignored, which is generous to every case.
